To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
delay discounting predicts behavioral ethanol sensitization in outbred Wistar-Sacre (WSC) mice and that this effect is independent of ethanol consumption and locomotor activity.
delay discounting and the rate of discounting predict behavioral sensitization to alcohol in outbred Wistar stock (WSC) mice.
the behavioral sensitization to repeated ethanol injections was predicted by the delay discounting of the same mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model of behavioral sensitization to a drug of abuse in mice, with a focus on the predictive value of delay discounting.
the effects of the drug ethanol on the central nervous system and behavior.
the effects of ethanol exposure during adolescence on ethanol consumption and preference in adulthood in outbred and selectively bred WSC mice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present study provides evidence that the behavioral sensitization to the effects of ethanol in outbred male mice can be predicted by delay discounting of ethanol rewards.
the results of the present study are not consistent with a role of the 5-HT1A receptor in the development and/or expression of the behavioral sensitization to repeated ethanol exposure.

the use of the delay discounting task in the study of alcoholism is promising and may be useful in predicting the development of alcoholism and the relapse to drinking, and may be used to assess the effectiveness of treatment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
delay discounting is an important factor for the development of behavioral sensitization in outbred Wistar-Sakai-Clearfield (WSC) mice.
